results.title: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies aged 65
results.content: Andy Taylor, whose guitar riffs helped shape Duran Duran's distinctive sound and propel the British band to global fame in the 1980s, has died aged 65 after a long battle with prostate cancer, the band and his family said Wednesday.

results.title: PSG's perfect Champions League record ends as Roma snatch 2-2 draw with late penalty
results.content: Donyell Malen's 78th-minute penalty earned Roma a 2-2 draw at Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday, ending the defending champions' perfect record in this season's Champions League. The result also halted PSG's 12-game winning streak in all competitions, leaving Real Madrid as the only team with a 100% record after five league-phase matches.

results.title: Le Pen party leaks: prefect dismissed, Paris deputy prosecutor placed under investigation
results.content: Two senior figures in France have been caught up in an investigation into suspected leaks to the far-right party of Marine Le Pen, the National Rally. The prefect of the Loiret, Hugues Moutouh, a former top official at the Interior Ministry, has been removed from his post after being suspected of passing on confidential information about investigations. And a deputy prosecutor in Paris, who was found at the party's headquarters during a police search, is now under administrative inquiry. FRANCE 24's Camille Knight reports.

results.title: Israeli lawmakers advance October 7 inquiry opposed by Netanyahu
results.content: Israel's new parliament on Wednesday took a first step to set up a state commission of inquiry into the security failures that led to Hamas's unprecedented October 7, 2023 attack, a move long opposed by caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.

results.title: New US tariffs: 'Trump lashing out really indiscriminately', expert says
results.content: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Dean Baker, Senior Economist at the Centre for Economic and Policy Research, says that "there has to be some mechanism for better coordinating China's involvement in the world trade system and ideally the US, the EU, Canada would have a common front, some clear ground rules that we could agree to, that China could agree to, to be mutually beneficial. It's not a step in that direction, we have President Trump lashing out really indiscriminately. It's very hard to see his approach being very productive".

results.title: Cape Town court shuts down Ramaphosa's Farmgate scandal
results.content: In tonight's edition, South Africa's president sidesteps an impeachment bid by the opposition. Also, we hear from some of the Malagasy women fighting for an overhaul of reproductive rights in their country. And in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, the CRP rebel group halts its advance after coming within dozens of kilometers of the northeastern city of Bunia.

results.title: Did GTA 6 really recreate Charlie Kirk's assassination?
results.content: Just days after its release, Grand Theft Auto 6 has become a vehicle for political misinformation. Viral footage falsely claims the game features a mission recreating Charlie Kirk’s assassination, while pro-Russian accounts are sharing fake screenshots containing anti-Ukrainian messages. Meanwhile, Russia’s own Defence Ministry has exploited the game's popularity to promote military recruitment. Vedika Bahl explains how GTA 6 is being used to push real political agendas in Truth or Fake.

results.title: Campaign rules for influencers? French regulator targets content creators
results.content: Ever since 1965 when the French first got to cast a ballot by universal suffrage for their president, they've valued campaign rules that guarantee ‘equal time’ for candidates. But what does equal time mean when you're closing in on 2027? Last week a bombshell announcement ahead of next Spring’s presidential elections: major online content creators will have to respect the same balanced air time rules as traditional TV and radio broadcasters during the campaign period. Here at France 24, we’re already testing the stopwatches and combing ove the guest list spreadsheets. Should podcasters, YouTubers and influencers be subjected to the same rules as us?

results.title: EU says 'strongly' rejects premise of new US tariffs
results.content: The EU said Wednesday that it rejected the premise of new tariffs on its exports proposed by the United States and expected Washington to stick by a deal struck with Brussels last year. The US unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

results.title: In boost for Netanyahu, judges question corruption trial charges
results.content: Judges in the long-running corruption trial of Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu handed his defence a major boost on Wednesday in recommending the prosecution drop one of the cases in which he is accused of bribery. The recommendations, which came as Israel's longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival, were immediately cheered by Netanyahu's right-wing allies who demanded the trial be brought to an end. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

results.title: Poland says will create no-fly zone at Ukraine border after repeated airspace violations
results.content: Poland will soon create a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border, a deputy defence minister announced on Wednesday, after several incursions into its airspace it blamed on Russia. Poland backs Ukraine as it fights off Russia's near five-year invasion and has repeatedly accused Moscow of seeking to target Kyiv's supporters with drone incursions and other methods. The no-fly zone is intended to allow Polish forces to quickly identify any Russian military aircraft and shoot them down if necessary. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.

results.title: US unveils proposed tariffs on major partners, including EU and China
results.content: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production -- the latest move by US President Donald Trump to remake Washington's trade relationships. The duties, proposed at up to 20 percent, come over allegations the economies "are promoting production and capacity divorced from the realities of demand and market principles," a senior US official said on condition of anonymity. FRANCE 24's Camille Knight.

results.title: The ‘French Milei’? Presidential candidate David Lisnard aims to reshape France’s right wing
results.content: Having secured reelection victory Wednesday as leader of France's mayors, Cannes Mayor David Lisnard turns once more to build on his recent bid for the Élysée. As his Nouvelle Énergie movement gains momentum, questions swirl over whether his campaign will reshape the French political landscape, or if his party will ultimately cosy up to the far right ahead of France’s 2027 race to the polls.

results.title: Turkey's deadly factory blast: 'Investing in safety costs more than letting people die'
results.content: An explosion at a steel factory on November 9 in Turkey's Aliaga, near Izmir, killed 19 people. This tragedy follows several others and highlights the issues surrounding workers’ safety in Turkey, our Observers say. They also condemn the repressive responses from the government and the company.

results.title: Paris takes on masculinist movements
results.content: As masculinist movements face their first major trial in Paris, the city has announced several initiatives to combat this ideology. The campaign aims to call attention to the real-world danger posed by misogynist groups online. FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler takes a closer look.

results.title: 'Free' land and thriving businesses: French village defies rural decline
results.content: As France's mayors gather in Paris for their annual convention, the decline in living standards and public services in both urban and rural areas is high on the agenda. Rural mayors, in particular, are concerned about the shrinking populations of their communities. But one small French town bucking the trend is Parlan, in the Cantal region, where the population has doubled and local services have flourished thanks to an offer of virtually free plots of land.

results.title: Moldova launches national preparedness campaign after drone incursions
results.content: Moldova is urging its citizens to prepare for emergencies as the war in neighbouring Ukraine brings new risks across its border. The “Moldova Ready” campaign, launched in Chisinau, includes a display of the remains of a drone carrying 52kg of explosives after it crashed in the country last month. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.

results.title: Top Spanish court closes case against Catalan separatist leader
results.content: Spain's Supreme Court has applied a controversial amnesty law to former Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont, closing criminal proceedings against him over his role in the region's failed 2017 independence bid. The ruling, which comes ahead of a snap general election on Sunday, marks the final step in the implementation of the amnesty law, passed by parliament in 2024.

results.title: Huang's return fails to dispel doubts as Nvidia shares drop
results.content: A rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia's chief executive faded on Tuesday, with the company's shares falling as doubts persisted over the probes he faces and the fate of the AI investment boom. After vaulting more than 30 percent on Monday following Huang's shock comeback, Nvidia fell almost six percent Tuesday. Huang resigned on November 12 over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.

results.title: US unveils proposed tariffs on major partners, including EU and China
results.content: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production – the latest move by US President Donald Trump to remake Washington's trade relationships. The new tariffs will need to undergo a period of public comment before taking effect. The new levies target some of the United States' largest trading partners. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

results.title: Iranian family seeks release of twin sisters facing death penalty and 25 years in prison
results.content: Twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi are awaiting their sentences in Iran. They were arrested in January 2026, at the age of just 19, for taking part in protests against the Iranian regime. Taraneh is facing the death penalty, while Romina has been sentenced to 25 years in prison. Their family has been campaigning for their release.

results.title: Russian casualties in Ukraine war: New reports suggest death toll as high as 700,000
results.content: New analysis of leaked Russian government data suggests some 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war against Ukraine. Independent Russian media outlets have updated their estimates of Moscow's military casualties after Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers obtained figures from the Russian statistics agency.

results.title: Iowa: Toxic dust fears as US Army blows up 10,000 pounds of explosives
results.content: An enormous explosion rang out across rural Iowa Tuesday as the US military carried out the controlled detonation of some 10,000 pounds of lead azide. US officials say the material, which was once used as a detonator in munitions, had become unstable and was at risk at risk of spontaneous explosion. But the risk of a toxic cloud of lead dust spreading out from the blast zone has caused public safety fears among locals.
